subject: Private deployment: DPA, subprocessors, customer-controlled keys and access boundaries (Arcadia Bank)

From: Emily Clark <emily.clark@arcadiabank.com>

Cc: Michael Lambert <michael.lambert@arcadiabank.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment DPA: subprocessors, BYOK, and access boundaries

Hi Priya —

Thanks for taking this call last week. As we look to move Arcadia Bank to a private deployment (VPC-hosted in our account or on-prem), legal and security flagged a few items we need clarified before procurement will sign the DPA. I captured the main asks in the attached PDF but wanted to summarize here: 

- Subprocessor inventory and the specific roles each subprocessor plays (monitoring, storage, telemetry, support).
- Customer-controlled keys: do you support BYOK / CMK in our KMS? If so, what access, if any, does Redwood staff have to plaintext keys or DEKs? Is there an escrow model?
- Operator access boundaries: what operational access is required for support (breakglass), and can that access be restricted to a named set of service accounts / IP ranges?
- Cross-border transfers: will any telemetry or logs ever leave the US without prior notice?
- Audit samples / evidence: they want to confirm how to get SOC2 or on-demand evidence for the private deployment.

We attached Arcadia_DPA_questions.pdf with examples. Procurement also asked whether we can add a clause that gives us 30 days notice of new subprocessors and a right to object for high-risk ones.

Can you please provide a concise response and any draft language we can add to the DPA? If preferable, happy to do a 30-min follow-up call next week.

Best,
Emily Clark
Head of Cloud Security
Arcadia Bank

Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA: subprocessors, BYOK, and access boundaries

Emily / Priya —

Following up with the technical detail Emily asked for. This is focused on our VPC-hosted and on-prem packages. TL;DR: we support true customer-controlled key models and limit operator access to metadata only. Details below — please feel free to share with your crypto team.

1) Keys and cryptographic model
- BYOK / CMK: Arcadia will provision the KEK (Key Encryption Key) in your cloud KMS or HSM. Redwood never persists plaintext KEKs.
- Data encryption: we encrypt data at rest with a Data Encryption Key (DEK). DEKs are wrapped by the KEK in the customer's KMS; Redwood stores only the wrapped DEK.
- Key operations: decryption of wrapped DEKs occurs inside the customer's VPC or on-prem environment where the KMS/HSM is reachable; our runtime does not export plaintext keys from the customer's environment.
- Escrow: we do not require key escrow for normal operations. If legal force compels access (e.g., regulatory order) we will surface the request per the DPA; we can include an escrow pathway only by exception and with explicit narrow conditions.

2) Operator access and breakglass
- Support: operational troubleshooting is done using ephemeral support sessions initiated by the customer or via pre-approved runbooks. We can restrict access to named service accounts/IP allowlists and require MFA + just-in-time authorization.
- No plaintext key access: Redwood engineers will not have access to plaintext DEKs/KEKs. Breakglass access is limited to log-level and feature flags; any session that elevates privilege is logged and requires an auditable approval flow.

3) Telemetry and logs
- Telemetry: runtime telemetry is configurable. For Arcadia we can restrict telemetry to aggregated metrics (latency, errors) and redact any payload-level content.
- Retention and egress: by default telemetry stays in the customer's region; no telemetry is sent outside the US without written consent.

4) Subprocessors
- Minimal list: for private deployments our subprocessor footprint is intentionally small — typically a cloud compute provider (if applicable), a managed observability vendor for optional hosted telemetry, and an on-call support provider.
- Notice: we support 30-day notice and a right to object to new subprocessors classified as high-risk.

5) Audit evidence
- For private deployments we provide SOC2 artifacts, on-demand evidence extracts, and can accommodate a scoped onsite or remote audit depending on contract.

I'll add suggested technical language to the privacy annex for your team to review. Happy to run a 30-min technical call to walk through live diagrams.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA: subprocessors, BYOK, and access boundaries

Emily —

Thanks for the clear list. A few legal points and suggested contract language we can include in the DPA / annex: 

1) Subprocessor clause: Redwood will provide at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice of new subprocessors and Customer shall have the right to reasonably object to such new subprocessors on the basis that the proposed subprocessor presents a material risk to Customer's regulated data. If an objection cannot be resolved within thirty (30) days, the parties will work in good faith to mitigate; if mitigation is not possible, Customer may terminate the affected services.

2) BYOK wording: Redwood will operate under a Customer-Managed Key model where (i) Customer retains sole control of the KEK in its KMS/HSM; (ii) Redwood will only store wrapped DEKs and will have no access to plaintext keys; (iii) any exception (e.g., escrow) will require explicit written agreement and scope.

3) Audit & evidence: Redwood will deliver SOC2 Type II reports and may provide on-demand evidence packages for the private deployment. If Arcadia requires additional audit rights (e.g., audit logs export or specific evidence samples), we can add a negotiated schedule with scope and cadence.

4) Cross-border and telemetry: Redwood will not transfer telemetry or customer logs outside the United States without prior written consent. We will add explicit geofencing language and a commitment to maintain telemetry retention windows as agreed.

I'll prepare a redline of the DPA with these clauses and send via DocuSign for review. Priya — please confirm preferred redline cadence and whether procurement needs a separate SOW for the on-prem option.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
